yad-avraham.1#_: (siman 119 seif 8) One suspected regarding a severe prohibition is suspected regarding a lighter one. In Rashba responsum siman 64 — one suspected regarding the severe is not suspected regarding the lighter, as a habitual sinner regarding circumcision is not a habitual sinner regarding slaughter. One must say his intent is as Beit Yosef brought in Taz — only regarding food matters do we say suspected for severe is suspected for light, but not for two categories; or as Taz in the name of the Perishah — only when he has benefit from it, but without benefit not; and what Shach wrote on the Perishah requires study. See Dagul MeRevavah who wrote on Shach that there is no proof from this alone that even though it is severe in karet penalty he still has time all his life, unlike other prohibitions where if he transgressed again there is no remedy. This is according to what is written in the gloss below at the beginning of Laws of Circumcision that every day he transgresses a karet prohibition and therefore he is not remedied for the past by circumcising afterward.
